precepts.text: Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. They that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly: their own personal gain. And by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple. If you are not studying, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody. It is warning you about fair speeches deceiving the hearts of the simple.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
Paul was warning, lest any man beguile you, deceive you, trick you. So he says in Romans: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly”: their own personal gain. They feed their own belly, their own mind.

Here is how they do it: “and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and lovely, beautiful speeches. If you ain't studying, especially you sisters, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody, and he's white. The scripture is warning you about fair speeches that deceive the hearts of the simple. Mark them and avoid them.

precepts.text: They that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly. Biggie said he only sold crack to feed his family; his stomach became his god. Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve: your look, conduct, speech, and character tell who your god is. If you are grotesquely overweight, outside a natural diet, you are your own god, the same self-worship as a birthday. The good news is you can control it.
precepts.point: Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: when am I going to eat, the things pleasing to the eyes and the flesh. Overindulging outside God's guidelines takes you out of the realm of discipline into the realm of Satan.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

precepts.text: Paul calls Priscilla and Aquila his helpers, who laid down their own necks for his life.
precepts.point: Aquila and Priscilla left Rome, met Paul in Corinth, travelled with him and taught Apollos the way of God more perfectly.

note.label: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.why:
When Paul came to Corinth he “found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. Rome commanded all the Israelites to leave. That is mass deportation, the same thing Claudius Caesar did back then that you see happening today with Trump and the ICE raids, and they are not raiding Europeans; they are going after the black and Hispanic communities.

But look what Aquila and Priscilla did after they were deported. They sailed with Paul into Syria, evangelizing and doing the work. When they heard Apollos, who only knew John, they “took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.” And Paul writes, “Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus: Who have for my life laid down their own necks”. That brother and his wife were not regular to Paul: they put their own heads on the chopping block for him.

The deportation was a divine mission. The Lord set them up to meet Paul, to teach Apollos, and to help spread the gospel. So don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord, and if they take your green card or your citizenship and send you back, it is of the Lord. Brother Nehemiah was deported from France for refusing to stop teaching, labelled an extremist, and now he is doing good in Ghana.

“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” Even the bad things happen for good, as the deportation did for Aquila and Priscilla. God has a purpose for every last one of us.

precepts.text: The Most High bruises Satan under the feet of His people; that is the bruising of the head.
precepts.point: It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” The Most High bruises Satan under the feet of His people. That is the bruising of the head.

“it shall bruise thy head” is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan. Satan bruises the heel, making Israel stumble; Christ bruises the head, and Satan goes under the feet of Israel.

precepts.text: Greet the church that is in their house, and Epaenetus the firstfruits of Achaia; congregations begin with the diligent few.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation, the sabbath as a holy convocation is still the order. You may have to travel, and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area.

That is how it began. Paul writes, “Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus”, and “Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.” The first assemblies met in houses, and Epenetus was the firstfruits of a whole region. Congregations begin with the diligent few, and that is how camps start: a church in a house, and a first one in the area.

precepts.text: The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly; Jacob bruises the head at the end of the world.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” The enmity set in the garden ends here: Satan bruised under the feet of Israel. They bruised Christ's heel; at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head.

That is the end of the Lord's war with Amalek from generation to generation. The seed that smote the hindmost coming out of Egypt, that rose again in Haman, that says it is Jews and is not, is made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and the God of peace bruises Satan under those same feet shortly.

precepts.text: Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine, and avoid them; once put out, that judgment is followed.
precepts.point: Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it. That is a judgment passed by the leaders, and to speak in that cause to decline after many, swaying people against it, is to wrest judgment. The marking ultimately comes from God.

precepts.text: Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
Under the kingdom, the prophet or dreamer of dreams who spoke to turn Israel away from the Lord was put to death. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated. What is done today is this: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

The one who speaks “to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in” is marked and avoided. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord. Those men and those women have to be put out from among the body. That is how “So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee” is kept today.

precepts.text: Those who serve their own belly deceive the hearts of the simple by good words and fair speeches; it is no longer the book and the straight commandments, just flattery and shade on the next man.
precepts.point: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Those who serve their own belly deceive the hearts of the simple by good words and fair speeches.

That is what the conversation becomes when the book of the law departs out of the mouth: it is no longer the book and the straight commandments, just flattery and shade on the next man. Slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech, fair speeches that deceive the simple.
